title: King Oliver's view of Lester; Good Night Sweetheart and a night in North Dakota
summary: Oliver said nobody could tell Lester anything about the horn and liked his Good Night Sweetheart; in North Dakota local musicians stayed up smoking and playing records with the few who didn't go to Canada.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I know King Oliver liked it. Did he ever say anything particularly, anything specific about Lester's phrasing or about his tone or about his melodic ideas? Did he ever go that far?

Yeah. He just said he was a good man. He said he was finished. King said, "Ain't nobody tell him nothin' about that horn." He knew that horn. King used to like to hear him play, "Good Night, Sweetheart." That used to be his going-home tune in them days.
And Prez used to be play on that?

Man, did he play! "Good night', sweetheart..." Tear it up. That was like in North Dakota. We was playing out there, man, and they had a bad house band up there. And them cats, man, the rest of the band went over to Canada. I didn't go, Prez didn't go, and who else... Three or four of us, we stayed there -- stayed in town. Because it

wasn't far. Where we was, wasn't over about maybe 100 miles or 75 miles to Winnipeg. So we stayed there, and waited for them to come back, because we had to play there another night. Man, them musicians in that hall was just like that, man. The news got around.

Then one cat who played tenor, he said to me, "Man, I'm not goin' home. I'm gonna stay with you all night." So they stayed with us all night. He went out and got a bag of good pot, we smoked pot all night and played records. They brought a lot of records over. We played Louis' records, you know records that were popular.
